ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, and $\angle A=100^\circ$. BD bisects $\angle ABC$. What is the measure of $\angle ADB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB=AC$ and $\angle A=100^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle ABC=\angle ACB=(180^\circ-100^\circ)\times \frac{1}{2}=40^\circ$,

$\because$ BD bisects $\angle ABC$,

$\therefore \angle ABD=\angle CBD=20^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle ADB=180^\circ-20^\circ-100^\circ=\boxed{60^\circ}$.
